terms.comment: Short in time and brief in speech (brevis esse, “to be brief”). Brevī is “shortly, soon”, and breviter “briefly”.

evidence: Phaedr. 3.7.1: quam dulcis sit lībertās, breviter prōloquar
terms.comment: The adverb of brevis: of speaking, in few words; of time, for a short while.

terms.gloss: for a short while, for a little while
evidence: Plaut. As. 5.2.30: paulisper manē (Lewis & Short s.v. paulisper)
Cic. Verr. 2.4.39: abesse ā domō paulisper māluit (Lewis & Short s.v. ab)
terms.comment: How long something lasts: a little while (see moment).

evidence: Traupman 88: for a short time, brevī tempore
terms.comment: “In a short time, shortly” (see soon): it says how soon, not how long. For “for a short time”, paulisper (above).

phrases.latin: omnia autem brevia tolerābilia esse dēbent, etiamsī magna sunt
phrases.english: anything short ought to be bearable, even if it is great

phrases.latin: Sapiēns quod petitur ubi tacet, breviter negat.
phrases.english: when a wise man says nothing to a request, he is saying no in short
